title: The Evils That Beset Our Path
description: The Evils That Beset Our Path in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 54, “Vanity of Life Eccl 2”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The e-vils that be-set our path Who can pre-vent or cure? We stand up-on the brink of death When most we seem se-cure.

lines: The evils that beset our path
Who can prevent or cure?
We stand upon the brink of death
When most we seem secure.
If we today sweet peace possess,
It soon may be withdrawn;
Some change may plunge us in distress,
Before tomorrow's dawn.
Disease and pain invade our health
And find an easy prey;
And oft, when least expected, wealth
Takes wings and flies away.
A fever or a blow can shake
Our wisdom's boasted rule;
And of the brightest genius make
A madman or a fool.
The gourds, from which we look for fruit,
Produce us only pain;
A worm unseen attacks the root,
And all our hopes are vain.
I pity those who seek no more
Than such a world can give;
Wretched they are, and blind, and poor,
And dying while they live.
Since sin has filled the earth with woe,
And creatures fade and die;
Lord wean our hearts from things below,
And fix our hopes on high.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
